In 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐆𝐨𝐝𝐟𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐈𝐈 (𝟏𝟗𝟕𝟒) nearly all of Vito’s dialogue is in Sicilian. Robert De Niro spent four months learning to speak Sicilian.

People respected Vito not only because they were afraid of him, but mostly because he was fair, wise, and cared about others. In the scenes from his younger years, we see how Vito earns people’s respect by helping them when no one else will. He listens to the problems of the people in his community and always tries to find a fair answer. Because of this, people see him as more than just a powerful man. They see him as someone who protects them and someone they can trust. When people come to ask him for help, they treat him with respect because they know he will listen and take them seriously.
